data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘atf’, meaning ‘to purify’. In Islamic tradition, this name signifies spiritual cleanliness and purification of the soul. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Atifat usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clean and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Her husband, Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, was also a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). After Talhah's death, Atifah remained devoted to Islam and was a source of inspiration for many.
